213	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
214	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
215	
216	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
217	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
218	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
219	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
220	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
221	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
222	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
223	
224	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
225	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
226	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
227	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
228	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
229	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
230	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
231	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
232	
233	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
234	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
235	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
236	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
237	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
238	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
239	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
240	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
241	
242	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
243	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
244	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
245	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
246	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
247	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
248	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
249	
250	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
251	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
252	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
253	No policy file is written implicitly.
254	
255	---
256	
257	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
258	
259	The major2 baseline artifact lives in the repository as tracked intent
260	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
261	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run3`
262	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
263	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
264	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
265	evaluator, provider, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
266	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
267	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
268	coverage (including each rule's recorded absence knowledge, §3), sorted unique matched entries and explicit unmatched occurrences.
269	Matched occurrences group only after equal fingerprint preimages and agreement
270	on every BaselineEntry field. Messages, parameters and citations remain on each
271	original finding. Unmatched findings retain their finding and subject identities;
272	they cannot be silently discarded or assigned a guessed stable fingerprint.
273	Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
274	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
275	`closureBundle` reference.
276	
277	**Detector identity.** A detector is identified by its evaluator emission contribution.
278	`detectorClosure` has exactly one row per distinct `contributionId` of the origin Plan's
279	`EvaluatorEmissionPlanV1` rule rows, disabled rules included: `detectorId` equals that
280	`contributionId`, and `closureId` and `semanticsMajor` are that row's `detectorClosure` and
281	`semanticsMajor`, which equal the policy rule's `ruleProgramRef` major. Two rows for one
282	contribution with a different closure or major refuse (`CONFIG.INVALID` /
283	`EVALUATION.FINDING_JOIN_REFUSED`). `BaselineEntry.detectorId` is the `contributionId` of the
284	entry rule's emission binding and is a member of `detectorClosure`; comparison `detectorId`
285	values use the same identity. Baseline admission checks these joins after recomputing
286	`baselineId`, so a self-consistently reminted rename of a detector identity is refused rather
287	than accepted as a different baseline.
288	
289	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
290	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
291	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
292	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
293	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
294	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
295	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
296	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
297	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
298	executed, whatever bytes are present.
299	
300	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
301	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
302	detector's authenticated compatibility listing names the baseline `closure2` as
303	exactly semantically compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`).
304	Security S1 binds this optional listing to the unique regular-file path
305	`.opensip/detector-compatibility.json` in the already admitted same `closure2`
306	tree. The listing uses `schemas/evaluator3/detector-manifest.schema.json`;
307	its exact retained byte length and SHA256 must match the signed tree file.
308	`closure.manifestDigest` continues to identify the component manifest body.
309	An absent reserved path means no declaration; a valid empty listing declares
310	no compatible peers; a present invalid, non-file or unavailable listing refuses
311	(`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `EVALUATION.PROJECTION_INPUT_INCOMPLETE`; the refusal
312	message is diagnostic only) and cannot silently become absence. The host admission origin is one of the
313	three current-trust paths above. Caller-provided compatibility or trust claims
314	do not supply that admission. Otherwise the baseline detector
315	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
316	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
317	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
318	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
319	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
320	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
321	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.
322	
323	**Baseline show.** `opensip baseline show [PATH]` admits the tracked artifact as above and reports,
324	for each descriptor pivot closure in order, its current-trust state: `missing` (no admitted record
325	or bytes), `revoked` (trust not admitted), `incompatible` (unsupported protocol major, or a platform
326	that is neither the host's nor `any`), or `available` with its trust origin (retained generation,
327	installed signed release or signed closure bundle). These states are data, not a failure.
328	
329	---
330	
331	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
332	
333	The major2 comparison result (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
334	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
335	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
336	
337	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
338	|---|---|---|---|---|
339	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
340	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
341	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
342	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
343	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
344	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
345	
346	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
347	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
348	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
349	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
350	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
351	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
352	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
353	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
354	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
355	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
356	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
357	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
358	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
359	
360	**Evidence for presence.** The fingerprint population is the union of B and
361	all admitted E0–E4 results, including fingerprints present only in a pivot.
362	A known matched finding establishes presence even when waived; waiver status
363	is a separate axis. Absence of a particular fingerprint requires complete
364	subject enumeration, determinate `emitWhen` proof roots for every selected
365	subject, and that fingerprint absent from the exact admitted emission set.
366	A known finding on another subject does not invalidate this negative knowledge.
367	All-false roots establish the stronger claim that the rule emitted no findings.
368	Required execution deficiencies still affect the overall Run and comparison
369	verdict; they do not retract a determinate per-rule fingerprint result.
370	An advisory `pass` alone does not establish absence. A false root may retain
371	unknown child witnesses under the published three-valued composition law;
372	those witnesses do not turn a determinate false root into unknown. Unknown
373	roots, incomplete enumeration, disabled evaluation and exhausted budgets do
374	not establish a negative result. Known hits remain usable in a partial result.
375	
376	**One presence-knowledge law on every side.** B, E0–E3 and E4 are each `true` (a known
377	matched occurrence), `false` or `null` (not known). `false` is either non-selection or
378	evaluated absence. Non-selection holds when that side's own policy does not enable the rule or
379	its ScopeDocument does not select the path: the side cannot emit the fingerprint, so the change
380	is attributed to the policy or scope axis that removed the selection. It is not an evaluated
381	negative result, and because B, E0 and E1 share the baseline selection it never becomes
382	`CODE-FIXED`. Evaluated absence is proved under the law above for that side's rule, including
383	the attested path extent and correspondence knowledge: an unmatched occurrence of the same rule
384	that might be the fingerprint leaves that side's presence `null`, because complete enumeration
385	with such an occurrence is not proof the fingerprint was fixed or never present. Such an
386	occurrence is related unless the paths differ or its retained subject kind, language and
387	qualified name provably differ from the fingerprint's subject key; where no stronger relation is
388	retained, the same-rule/same-path barrier applies. No fingerprint is ever minted for an unmatched
389	occurrence, and a known matched hit stays `true`. The absence of a matched current hit is not by itself a known
390	`false`: for an enabled rule selecting the path, incomplete or unknown enumeration, unknown
391	roots and an exhausted budget leave E4 `null`. B is evaluated-absent for a non-entry only when
392	the baseline's `RuleCoverage.absenceKnowledge` for that rule is `complete-hit-set`, recorded at
393	adoption by the same law and no retained baseline `unmatchedOccurrences` row has the same rule
394	and path (those rows carry no subject identity); B non-selection is read from the embedded
395	baseline policy and ScopeDocument. The baseline artifact records per-rule knowledge, not a per-path extent. An entry whose first attributable change along B→E4 would rest on a `null`
396	value is `INDETERMINATE` with `current-absence-unknown` (unknown E4) or
397	`baseline-absence-unknown` (unknown B), never `CODE-FIXED`, `UNCHANGED` or `CODE-NET-NEW` by
398	default. A change already established between known values before the unknown value keeps its
399	classification, so a known `CODE-NET-NEW` still fails. Rule coverage, evidence and execution
400	deficiencies remain independent of this knowledge.
401	
402	**Indeterminate reason selection (closed).** An entry publishes exactly one
403	`indeterminateReason`, the first applicable in this order: (1) `pivot-reevaluation-unavailable`
404	when a changed axis's pivot presence is `null` (E0 for a changed detector map, E1 policy, E2
405	scope, E3 waivers), whether that pivot was not bound or was bound without presence knowledge,
406	including a correspondence barrier on that pivot; (2) the evidence axis, evaluated per declared
407	`evidenceUse` in declaration order: `required-evidence-unavailable`, then for a gating rule
408	`evidence-availability-changed` or `evidence-content-changed`; (3) the detector disposition's
409	own reason when its method is `indeterminate`; (4) `baseline-absence-unknown` when the first
410	attributable change rests on a `null` B; (5) `current-absence-unknown` when it rests on a `null`
411	E4. Whole-comparison reasons perform no comparison and emit no entries.
412	
413	**An unmatched baseline occurrence is not proven absence.** A baseline that retains an unmatched
414	occurrence of a rule on a path (for example a symbol whose detector projection was unavailable)
415	does not prove that a fingerprint of that rule on that path was absent. A fingerprint present
416	only on a pivot stays in the comparison universe, the baseline's gating unmatched obligation
417	remains a `correspondence-incomplete` deficiency, and the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
418	(`baseline-absence-unknown`), not `CODE-NET-NEW`. A genuinely complete baseline that selects the
419	path, records complete absence knowledge and retains no such unmatched occurrence proves

473	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
474	
475	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
476	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
477	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
478	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
479	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
480	
481	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
482	|---|---|---|
483	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
484	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
485	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
486	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
487	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
488	
489	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
490	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
491	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
492	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
493	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
494	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
495	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
496	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
497	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
498	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
499	
500	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
501	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
502	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
503	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
504	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
505	
506	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
507	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
508	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
509	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
510	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
511	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
512	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
513	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
514	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
515	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
516	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
517	but never feeds a predicate.
518	
519	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
520	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
521	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
522	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
523	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
524	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
525	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.
526	
527	**A repair evidence requirement over one of these two relations has its own
528	owning outcome law**, `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law`
529	(§6). It is separate from native §4.6 because these relations mint no `fact2` and
530	carry no Coverage, and **each kind is projected through its own payload**: a
531	runtime requirement reads `observability`, `observationWindow` and
532	`observedPopulation`; a history requirement reads `revisionRange` and
533	`collectionScope`, which are its bounds fields; `HistoryPayloadV1` also carries
534	subjects and has no runtime observation-window, population or observability
535	fields. Neither kind may report the other's outcomes.
536	
537	**A repair target is a fingerprint, not a path, and the join is published.**
538	`RepairPlanDescriptor.targets` are `finding-key2:` **fingerprints**, while
539	`RuntimeSubject` is keyed by `{path, symbol?}` and `HistorySubject` by `{path}`.
540	The deterministic projection is
541	`imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law/targetSubjectProjection`:
542	each target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by `evidenceRunId` (preview
543	already refuses one that is not); that `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of
544	the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention is
545	`preimage` and whose bytes are therefore re-hashed at Run closure; and its
546	`subjectKey` supplies the path and qualified name used for matching. The projection
547	does not classify the target by `kind`, whose vocabulary is not closed here. A
548	runtime row matches on path and, if it names a symbol, on qualified name; another
549	symbol's row does not match. A runtime row with no symbol and every history row
550	provide **file** granularity, with `granularityWidenedToFile` disclosed in the
551	projection and successful outcome. A symbol-naming runtime row provides the
552	format's path-and-name granularity, not an exact match of the whole subject key:
553	neither format distinguishes `language`, `kind` or `discriminator`. Distinct
554	findings can therefore project to the same observation. This stated limit applies
555	to every such projection; it cannot establish execution or non-execution of a
556	particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity. More than one
557	matching subject **refuses**: an ambiguous projection is not resolved by choosing
558	one. A target with no matching subject is unsupported — never satisfied, and never
559	read as evidence of non-use.
560	
561	Five limits carry over and are enforced rather than assumed.
562	**Satisfied does not mean positive**: `observed-hit` is positive execution
563	evidence and `observable-unhit` is *bounded negative* evidence, both can satisfy,
564	and the disclosure records which did. **No imported observation establishes a
565	universal negative** — one window is not universal non-use — and imported evidence
566	can never *by itself* establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe
567	`delete`/`replace`, and it can never **improve** that gate either: the gate reads
568	only the **native** `ClosedWorldV2` records the §6 relevance rule selects from the
569	evidence Run, and no imported observation is one of them.
570	It may still be an **additional required condition** alongside an
571	already-established native basis, so it is wrong to say it never affects
572	applicability; an unsatisfied imported requirement makes an otherwise-eligible
573	plan inapplicable. **Whole-versus-partial** is decided by the requirement's
574	`completeness` field: `complete` needs every plan target supported,
575	`partial-acceptable` at least one. That enum already existed, but **this reading of
576	it for an imported requirement over plan targets is selected here** and was not
577	previously published. A target that is unobservable or outside the history
578	collection scope therefore only names the cause *more precisely when the support
579	test fails* — it does not veto a lawful `partial-acceptable` requirement that has a
580	supported target. **Bounds are separate from support**: an insufficient observation
581	window or revision range applies under both completeness values, because it is a
582	property of the observation rather than of the target count. And **required versus
583	optional** stays where `evidenceUse` puts it — an optional absence remains the
584	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` disclosure and is satisfied *by absence* rather than
585	by evidence. That declaration reaches the requirement boundary as a **typed
586	boolean**; a non-boolean refuses, so there is no `unknown` state to default and no
587	falsy value is read as optional.

591	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
592	
593	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV2` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
594	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
595	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
596	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
597	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
598	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
599	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
600	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
601	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
602	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
603	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
604	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
605	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
606	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
607	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
608	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
609	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
610	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
611	
612	Glob matching follows the single [portable glob contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/glob-pattern-contract.v1.md): full-string, case-sensitive matching; terminal whole-segment `**` includes a filename, so `src/**` matches `src/index.ts`. The same predicate applies to policy field filters and host path scopes. Each containing contract continues to own its defaults and include/exclude combination law.
613	The compiled RuleProgramV2 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
614	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
615	The exact endpoint, native field projection and imported test-filter grammars
616	are in that policy schema and the incorporated atom contract. Identity §4 and
617	the composition contract own independent subject enumeration, complete tree
618	replay, full finding emission, waiver membership and budget semantics. Declared
619	required evidence remains distinct from retained nonblocking branch diagnostics.
620	
621	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
622	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
623	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
624	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
625	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
626	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
627	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly. `opensip policy show` resolves the tracked
628	policy and waiver documents at the admitted trust-clock date and reports the policy, its digest,
629	the effective waiver set, its digest and the resolution disclosure.
630	
631	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. Its input is `PolicyTestSuiteV2`
632	(`schemaMajor` 2, [`schemas/evaluator3/policy-test.schema.json`](../../../coop/design-corrections/workflows/schemas/evaluator3/policy-test.schema.json)):
633	a candidate `PolicyDocumentV2`, unchanged `WaiverSetV1` waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only
634	overrides of candidate rules and cases with typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage,
635	available evidence kinds) or a bounded source fixture. The retained `PolicyTestSuiteV1` (candidate
636	`PolicyDocumentV1`) is the historical workflow1 input only. This is a breaking input change for
637	`policy test`, not a relabel: a retained major-1 suite and its result stay historical evidence and are
638	not re-evaluated under this profile. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
639	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
640	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers) under the current policy resolver and
641	atom law, including endpoint, kind applicability and the registered filter projections. The facts
642	fixture has an explicit representation law in that schema: a filter field or imported observation it
643	cannot carry (the endpoint universe domain, `testResult`, `exitStatus`, test-execution and test-case
644	observations) is unknown, and the absence of an imported row never proves absence. An unknown result
645	for an enumerated subject lists the rule in `indeterminateRules` and leaves an affected finding or
646	no-finding expectation `indeterminate` unless a known finding decides it; known findings, strong
647	Kleene and gating are unchanged. Sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
648	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
649	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
650	The result stays `PolicyTestResultV1` (`policytest2:`) and records candidate and effective digests, resolver
651	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
652	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
653	Admission precedes evaluation, in this order. A suite or candidate policy of another major is
654	`request-rejected` (exit 2) `REQUEST.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` with `EVALUATION.MIXED_OUTPUT_MAJOR`, the
655	current policy major refusal; it is never relabelled, coerced or grammar-classified. Every other refusal
656	is `request-rejected` (exit 2) with `errorCode`
657	`CONFIG.INVALID`, the D9 rejection cause `config-invalid`; the `DomainDetail` is a separate
658	registered code. A candidate policy carrying a member that no closed `PolicyDocumentV2` alternative
659	declares at that position, or a string where every closed alternative at that position is
660	an object (a string expression), is `POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`. Any other `PolicyTestSuiteV2`
661	admission failure, a fixture fact whose resolution is not a rung of its registered relation or whose
662	universe is not a registered policy universe token, or an override of a non-candidate rule or with the
663	wrong value type carries the
664	shared registered `CONFIG.INVALID` detail; the public detail registry row is registered by
665	security, and the native route registry reuses the same detail for external configuration. An
666	admitted suite whose candidate policy or waivers the current resolver refuses terminates the same way
667	with the resolver's detail (`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `POLICY.UNKNOWN_RULE`,
668	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE`); its `resolverAccepted=false` result records the refusal but is
669	not a query carrier. A candidate rule whose `subjectEnumeration.universe` is not a token of the closed
670	evaluator profile policy universe map (composition contract §2: `typescript`, `rust`, `syntax`) is such a
671	`POLICY.UNKNOWN_RULE` refusal. Declared required evidence absent from a case never suppresses a known
672	finding: the rule keeps its required-evidence deficiency in `indeterminateRules`, and a live unwaived gating
673	finding still makes the verdict `fail` (composition contract §5 and §9.5).

676	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds

701	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
702	
703	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
704	
705	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
706	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
707	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
708	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
709	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
710	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
711	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
712	`run3`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
713	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
714	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
715	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
716	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
717	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
718	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes. In the evaluator3 profile the plan is
719	`repair:2` (`evidenceRunId` `run3`): the evaluator3 workflow owner joins the targets to matched
720	`finding-key2` fingerprints of the retained evidence Run (workflow projection contract §5), builds
721	the descriptor at that major and admits the plan before returning it. The historical major-1 plan
722	keeps its own constructor and schema, and neither is relabelled into the other.

862	  `common.schema.json#/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency` because this bundle
863	  resolves only its own URNs.
864	* **Imported plane** — `runtime-observation` and `history-change`. Those relations
865	  mint no `fact2` and have no Coverage entry, so `sufficiency_v2` has nothing to
866	  range over and is not asked. Their outcomes are owned by
867	  `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law` and mirrored
868	  as `common.schema.json#/$defs/ImportedRequirementDeficiency`; every member names
869	  an already-published import condition and is bound to the payload field that
870	  grounds it, and each kind reports only the outcomes **its own** payload can
871	  ground — enforced at **both** the producer and this admission (§4). The
872	  requirement record gains no field: plan `targets` supply the per-target scope
873	  through the published fingerprint projection, `completeness` decides
874	  whole-versus-partial under the reading selected in §4, and `evidenceUse` supplies
875	  required-versus-optional as a typed boolean. The bounded observation demand is
876	  owned by the **admitted recipe closure** named by `recipe.closureId` — `RecipeRef`
877	  carries no such wire field and none is claimed.
878	
879	The two vocabularies are **disjoint**, and a cross-plane value — a native
880	requirement claiming `import-unmapped-only`, or an imported one claiming
881	`resolution-incomplete` — is refused at admission, as is an outcome of the wrong
882	imported **kind**, such as a history range cause on a runtime relation. This schema
883	**deliberately leaves the authoritative registry lookup to admission**: it admits
884	either vocabulary and does not attempt to reproduce the relation registries, which
885	it could not fetch rows from in any case. That is a design choice about where the
886	authority lives, not a limitation of JSON Schema — a schema *can* branch on a
887	property's `const`/`enum` even where the base type is a broader string — and
888	duplicating a registry as schema conditionals would create exactly the drift this
889	contract set avoids elsewhere. The division is stated rather than implied.
890	
891	The value carried is the **satisfaction/deficiency projection** of its producer's
892	result, not that result: `sufficiency_v2` also returns `causes` on both branches
893	and may return `disclosures` on a failing branch. Those are producer result arrays
894	and are fields of no retained record; what is retained is the evidence the
895	evaluation read, so the projection drops nothing that was retained. Presence is **typed**: `deficiency` is **required
896	exactly when `satisfied` is false** and **forbidden when it is true**, `satisfied`
897	must be an actual boolean, and an explicit `null` is refused in both branches
898	because a present key with a null value is not an absent key. Both boundaries — the
899	schema and the preview admission — decide that same law and are held equal on an
900	enumerated shape table. The field previously named
901	`D9Deficiency`, which cannot express four of the nine outcomes its only producer
902	emits — `derivation-policy-unmet`, `external-consumers-unknown`,
903	`input-closure-incomplete` and `resolution-incomplete` — leaving three conforming
904	readings and no document choosing between them: write the D9-mapped value, which
905	is `verdict-indeterminate` for **all four** and so cannot tell
906	`resolution-incomplete` (the outcome §4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal
907	negative under `unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid` over an affected target, and the one
908	a destructive unused-code recipe turns on) from three unrelated causes; write the
909	sufficiency value and be schema-invalid; or omit the field and drop the
910	disclosure. Retyping this one per-requirement field is the correction.
911	`D9Deficiency` is **unchanged** and still carries every whole-Run and
912	comparison-step termination — three of its members name evaluation, baseline and
913	query outcomes no per-requirement evaluation can produce — and the public D9
914	route for a Run carrying such a requirement is still native §10's. The value is a
915	**disclosure, not an authorization**: `applicable` is false whenever any
916	requirement is unsatisfied, the exact cause is carried into that requirement's
917	unmet precondition so two different causes are two different remedies, the
918	evidence authority remains the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`, and any edit
919	to the value mints a different `repairPlanId` that no authorization names.
920	That unmet precondition is emitted once per unsatisfied requirement and carries
921	the existing `REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE` code, which here says that the
922	evidence Run cannot supply what this repair requires and asserts nothing about the
923	Run having been purged or lost — `evidence.purged` and `evidence.missing` keep
924	their own distinct meaning in query results. Preview therefore reaches that one
925	code by two routes, the retained-availability and replayable-assurance failure of
926	the first paragraph above and this per-requirement insufficiency, and the remedy
927	is what tells them apart: the retention entry's remedy names the Run-level
928	restoration that route needs, while the per-requirement entry's remedy names that
929	requirement's `relation`, `minResolution`, evidence plane and exact `deficiency`.
930	`EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` remains the typed cause carrier: no
931	per-deficiency detail code is minted, because the closed public registry is not
932	where a per-requirement outcome vocabulary belongs. An unsatisfied requirement
933	with an empty `unmetPreconditions` is **not** a conforming projection — the schema
934	alone admits that shape, and the emission is decided at admission, the same
935	division of labour already stated for the deficiency vocabulary.
936	
937	`RepairPlanDescriptor.closedWorld` is a deterministic **five-field display
938	summary** of the selected records — `deadCodeRepairEligible`, `exportsClosed`,
939	`entryPointsRecognized`, `nonliteralLoading`, `externalConsumers` — and
940	`repair.schema.json` closes it at exactly those five, so a literal copy of
941	`ClosedWorldV2`, which carries seven, is refused there. It is **not** a native
942	producer record and does not claim to be one: a fieldwise reduction over several
943	entries may combine members that no single producer emitted together. That is
944	acceptable only because the record carries **no authority**. The reduction is
945	total and fixed:
946	
947	* `deadCodeRepairEligible` is the conjunction over the selected records, and
948	  `false` when none were selected.
949	* each remaining member takes the **least-closed** value present, ordering
950	  `closed ≺ open ≺ unknown`, `all ≺ partial ≺ none`, `none ≺ present`,
951	  `none-declared ≺ possible ≺ unknown`.
952	* **absence is folded in, not hidden.** When any relevant universe retains no
953	  native Coverage, or any selected binding's ownership of an unsafe path is
954	  unresolved, the reduction additionally folds in the sentinel below, so the
955	  summary cannot read as closed while eligibility is refused for that absence.
956	
957	With nothing selected the same rule yields the **five-field least-closed display
958	sentinel**, which is exactly
959	`{deadCodeRepairEligible: false, exportsClosed: unknown, entryPointsRecognized:
960	none, nonliteralLoading: present, externalConsumers: unknown}`. It is **not an
961	"all-unknown" record** and must not be described as one: only two members are
962	`unknown`; the other three are a false boolean and the least-closed pole of each
963	of the two enums that cannot spell absence. `ClosedWorldV2` has no `unknown`
964	member for `entryPointsRecognized` (`all|partial|none`) or `nonliteralLoading`
965	(`none|present`), so their poles stand in. That is this display rule applied
966	uniformly — **not** an observation that entry points went unrecognised or that
967	nonliteral loading was seen — and widening the native enum is not this section's
968	to do.
969	
970	**The summary grants no evidence authority of its own.** **No member of it is
971	authoritative, the boolean included**; the authority is the full native selection
972	above. It is never an input to
973	the gate, which reads the full selected records including the two members the
974	summary does not carry. No edit to it can make a plan applicable, since the whole
975	descriptor is the preimage of `repairPlanId`
976	(`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) and apply requires a security
977	authorization bound to that exact `repairPlanId`, base snapshot and project.
978	Preview is a Query-class step and is **not** authorization: `applicable=true` is
979	a disclosure that the preconditions held, and trust, consent, current-snapshot
980	equality and that bound authorization are all still required at apply.
981	
982	**Create-only plans still carry a summary.** A plan with no `delete` and no
983	`replace` activates no gate, and an ineligible closed world alone adds **no**
984	unmet precondition to it. It still **reads** the selection and still **builds**
985	the five-field member — the member is `required` in the descriptor and the whole
986	descriptor is the `repairPlanId` preimage, so a create-only plan does not escape
987	the question, it only escapes the veto. It is summarised by the same reduction,
988	falling back to the **five-field least-closed sentinel above** — not an
989	all-unknown record — when the Run retains no relevant native Coverage at all, so
990	the descriptor, and therefore `repairPlanId`, is deterministic for a create-only
991	plan exactly as for any other.
992	
993	**What this changes, stated precisely.** The identity *recipe* and the descriptor
994	*shape* are unchanged: the same five member names, the same `additionalProperties:
995	false`, the same schema majors, and `repairPlanId` is still
996	`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)` over the whole descriptor. What moves is
997	the *value* this member takes, so an implementation that previously used a
998	caller-selected record may now mint a different `repairPlanId` for the same
999	request. **No equality of `repairPlanId` is claimed across different Runs**:
1000	`evidenceRunId` is part of the preimage, so a different Run is a different plan
1001	identity however similar its evidence. Equality holds only where every descriptor
1002	input, that Run included, is identical.
1003	
1004	The authority stays the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`. No claim is made here
1005	that a later step re-reads it — `repair verify` seals a **new** Run over the
1006	freshly re-snapshotted tree (`appliedSnapshotId` → `verifiedSnapshotId`) and
1007	compares remaining and net-new findings; it does not re-open the original evidence
1008	Run.
1009	
1010	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
1011	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
1012	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
1013	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
1014	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
1015	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
1016	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
1017	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
1018	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
1019	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
1020	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
1021	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
1022	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
1023	
1024	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
1025	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
1026	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
1027	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
1028	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
1029	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
1030	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
1031	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
1032	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
1033	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
1034	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
1035	
1036	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
1037	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
1038	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
1039	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
1040	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
1041	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
1042	and remains retained if verification fails.

1046	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
1047	
1048	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
1049	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
1050	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
1051	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
1052	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
1053	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
1054	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
1055	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
1056	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
1057	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
1058	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
1059	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
1060	
1061	**Argv digest.** `argvDigest` is the lowercase hexadecimal raw SHA-256 of `C(argv)`, where
1062	`C` is product canonical JSON (identity-and-evidence §3) and `argv` is the exact ordered array
1063	of argument strings actually selected for the spawn. Every element stays a separate array
1064	member, preserving order, repeated elements and any empty string an owning schema admits; no
1065	shell-joined, quoted, normalized or PATH-resolved surrogate is digested. The recipe is the same
1066	wherever the digest binds, `RepoExecutionGrantV2.argvDigest` (security S10) and
1067	`TestPayloadV1.argvDigest`: host test execution digests `TestExecutionStepParams.argv`, native
1068	preparation digests the host-selected preparation argv of its grant, and an independently
1069	prepared test payload digests the argument array its adapter recorded.
1070	
1071	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
1072	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
1073	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
1074	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). Every effect value must equal the selected
1075	truth-table profile row (security S10). The selected `permission-truth-tables.v9` profile has
1076	no measured platform-primitive row, so `ENFORCED-PLATFORM:<primitiveId>` cannot be claimed in
1077	this profile and is not a member of `TestExecutionStepParams` `EnforcementValue`; security
1078	`EnforcementV1` keeps that vocabulary for a future measured primitive, which requires a
1079	successor truth-table profile and test-execution schema. The mandatory sentence before spawn is
1080	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
1081	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
1082	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
1083	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
1084	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
1085	are the supported alternative.

1090	
1091	`workflows/command-inventory.v3.json` is the single intended inventory,
1092	validated by `workflows/schemas/evaluator3/command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
1093	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
1094	
1095	| Group | Commands |
1096	|---|---|
1097	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
1098	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |

1103	Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
1104	Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
1105	may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
1106	its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.

1109	reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
1110	one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
1111	static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
1112	disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
1113	parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
1114	carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
1115	`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
1116	`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and

1118	and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are

1126	`run-id` is explicitly null in the projection's non-authoritative case,
1127	never a fabricated Run. Required-output failure still follows the law below.

1129	before a renderer consumes it: every field has its schema-admitted value,
1130	including an explicit null only where that field permits it. A missing field
1131	or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault, not an empty
1132	result or a successful partial rendering: `operational-failed`, exit 4,
1133	`faultCause=delivery-required`, `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`. If a Run was already
1134	committed, the termination retains its RunId and the after-commit detail below;

1138	projection helper raising `KeyError`; that exception alone is not a public

1147	**Query.** The twenty closed operations remain read-only. The current schema is
1148	`workflows/schemas/evaluator3/graph-query.schema.json` major 3. The incorporated
1149	[query projection contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/workflows/query-projection-contract.v3.md)
1150	owns the complete selection, endpoint, result, ordering, traversal, continuation
1151	and evidence-disclosure laws for `graph.neighbors`, `graph.path` and `graph.reach`.
1152	It does not replace the artifact-specific owners of the other seventeen operations.
1153	
1154	Graph requests may select `run3`, `snapshot2` or `latest`; before traversal they
1155	resolve to one concrete retained Run and an exact fact-view selection. An empty
1156	resolver domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`; ambiguity is a typed refusal. A graph
1157	response never echoes an unresolved `latest` alias as its resolved view. Endpoint
1158	identity includes the selected universe and native identity, so equal paths in
1159	different analysis universes cannot silently collapse. Results retain their fact
1160	provenance. Database row IDs and backend iteration order are not public identity
1161	or ordering rules.
1162	
1163	The bounded graph contract distinguishes a page boundary from exhaustion of the
1164	logical operation. Page size is at most 1,000; produced items at most 100,000;
1165	semantic depth at most 64; visited nodes at most 1,000,000. `maxDepth` defines the
1166	requested search distance, not an implicit promise of unbounded reachability.
1167	`completeness=required` refuses genuinely unfinished work at an operation bound
1168	with `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3); exactly reaching a limit with no owed work is
1169	not incompleteness. Best-effort reports any truncation explicitly. A continuation
1170	can page only the bounded result and never reset the work budget; its last page
1171	can remain truncated with no cursor. Total-count disclosure distinguishes an
1172	exact total from a lower bound.
1173	
1174	A continuation binds the project, concrete retained Run and fact views,
1175	operation, effective parameters, ordering and position. Publication of a newer
1176	Run cannot change that selection. Index loss permits rebuilding from the same
1177	available closure; unavailable retained evidence or incompatible continuation
1178	inputs cause the contract's typed refusal, never a switch to a newer Run.
1179	
1180	For the graph operations, traversal completion and retained evidence sufficiency
1181	are separate typed disclosures, including relevant Coverage, scope, deficiency
1182	and resolution limitations. Exhausting stored edges, returning no rows, or
1183	ending pagination cannot itself prove that no callers exist. Any such finding
1184	must retain the existing native/evaluator authority and citations. All query
1185	responses carry their owned view, evidence disclosure, availability and `advisory`;
1186	the other seventeen operations retain their existing Coverage field. `advisory` is
1187	true exactly for `comparison.diff`, `candidate.list`, `inspection.show` and
1188	`review.brief`. The three graph operations are not advisory and do not seal a Run.
1189

1191	`truncated`, `total-items`, `termination-class` and `query-response`. The last is
1192	the **complete owner-admitted GraphQueryResponseV1**, including the full context,

1195	that response. Graph evidence is not reduced to a synthetic Coverage scalar.
1196	The first four scalar fields are exact projections of the response context;
1197	`termination-class` comes from the enclosing command's actual StepTermination.
1198	If the response carries termination, its entire object must equal the enclosing
1199	termination. The envelope and response must identify the same project. Missing
1200	required query disclosure follows the existing required-delivery fault law.

1501	
1502	| Rule | Statement |
1503	|---|---|
1504	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1505	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1506	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1507	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1508	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1509	
1510	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1511	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1512	
1513	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1514	|---|---|---|---|
1515	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1516	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1517	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1518	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1519	
1520	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1521	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1522	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1523	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1524	
1525	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1526	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1527	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1528	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1529	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1530	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1531	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1532	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1533	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1534	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1535	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1536	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1537	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1538	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1539	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1540	
1541	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1542	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1543	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1544	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1545	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1546	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1547	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1548	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1549	which two paths share a basename refuses
1550	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1551	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1552	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1553	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1554	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1555	
1556	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1557	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1558	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1559	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1560	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1561	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1562	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1563	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).

1565	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1566	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1567	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1568	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1569	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1570	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.

1572	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`

1636	
1637	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1638	
1639	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1640	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1641	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1642	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1643	
1644	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1645	
1646	| Field | Rule |
1647	|---|---|
1648	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1649	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1650	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1651	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1652	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1653	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1654	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1655	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1656	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1657	
1658	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1659	
1660	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1661	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1662	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1663	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1664	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1665	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1666	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1667	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1668	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1669	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1670	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1671	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1672	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1673	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1674	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1675	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1676	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1677	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1678	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1679	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1680	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1681	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1682	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1683	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1684	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1685	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1686	  syntax analysis.
1687	
1688	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1689	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1690	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1691	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

1693	### 3.2 Custody and transport
1694	
1695	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1696	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
1697	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
1698	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
1699	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
1700	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
1701	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.

1703	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1704	
1705	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1706	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1707	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1708	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1709	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1710	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1711	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
1712	
1713	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1714	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1715	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):

1867	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1868	
1869	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1870	
1871	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1872	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1873	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1874	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1875	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1876	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1877	
1878	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1879	
1880	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1881	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1882	
1883	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1884	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1885	
1886	```
1887	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1888	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1889	```
1890	
1891	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1892	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1893	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1894	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1895	
1896	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1897	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1898	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1899	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1900	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1901	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1902	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1903	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1904	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1905	
1906	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1907	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1908	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1909	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1910	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1911	against a value the provider never supplied.
1912	
1913	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1914	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1915	
1916	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1917	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1918	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1919	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1920	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1921	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1922	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1923	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1924	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1925	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1926	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1927	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1928	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1929	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1930	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1931	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1932	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1933	
1934	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1935	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1936	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1937	
1938	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1939	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1940	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1941	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1942	
1943	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1944	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1945	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record

1948	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1949	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.

2339	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2340	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.

2346	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2347	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2348	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2349	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.

2352	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2353	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2354	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only
2355	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2356	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2357	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2358	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2359	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It

2368	correctly against an entry a conforming native provider would never have emitted —
2369	a defective or non-conforming provider, and the defensive fixture below. No
2370	*imported* route is offered as an example and none is implied: imported evidence
2371	is a separate plane that mints no `ViewEntryV3` at all (§7, workflows §4), so it
2372	could not supply one of these values, and inventing such a path to explain the
2373	wider domain would be fabricating a mechanism. The named regression case
2374	`sufficiency-v2-confidence-floor-precedes-one-rung-existential-shortcut` is
2375	exactly that: a hand-built evaluator input, **not** a `ViewEntryV3` and **not**
2376	provider emission, exercising `clones` at 100000 against a floor of 900000 so that
2377	the removed early exit cannot come back. Its 100000 is therefore no counterexample
2378	to the emission law and is not evidence that any native provider emits such a
2379	value; it is a defensive fixture for the evaluator, and this contract makes no

2386	### 5.1 Principal class `repository-code` and its joins (R4)
2387	
2388	The security contract S10 registers principal class `repository-code`
2389	(`RepoExecutionGrantV2`, execution classes `build-script | proc-macro |
2390	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and
2391	checked by schema constants:
2392	
2393	| Where | Spelling | Role |
2394	|---|---|---|
2395	| security S10 / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.principalClass` | `repository-code` | principal class of the admitted grant |
2396	| foundation `identity-schemas.v3#semantic-grant.principals[].kind` / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.semanticGrantPrincipalKind` | `trusted-repository-code` | Plan-bound semantic projection `{kind, closureId (tool closure), ownerSourceDigest (owner file manifest)}` with `analysisOperations ∋ prepare-code` |

2398	
2399	The **authority grant** is the operational `authorizationRef`
2400	(`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)`, the workflow's `securityGrantRef`):
2401	it is excluded from the Plan descriptor and from every content identity
2402	(`authorized-execution-interactive-with-declared-owner-disclosed` checks
2403	`authorizationRefInPlan=false`). The **semantic grant projection** is what the Plan
2404	binds. A universe with `preparedResolution=imported-inert` projects only
2405	`read-import`; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code`. Prepared semantic
2406	availability therefore never implies that this host holds or held an execution
2407	grant (`prepared-imported-inert-implies-no-host-execution-grant`).
2408	
2409	The principal, identified by `{projectId, snapshotId, ownerKey,
2410	ownerFileManifestSha256, toolchainDigest}`, is **outside** the first-party TCB.
2411	Executing it in-host is a disclosed trusted-code execution of code the user chose
2412	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a
2413	platform primitive is enforced. The security owner supplies the revocation clock
2414	and cancellation carrier (H-2).
